primary_claim: On Auditing Sabotage Bench, a new benchmark of 9 ML research codebases with sabotaged variants, neither frontier LLMs nor LLM-assisted humans reliably detect research sabotage: the best auditor (Gemini 3.1 Pro) achieves AUROC 0.77 with only a 42% top-1 fix rate, and LLM-generated sabotages partially evade even same-capability LLM monitors.

effect.metric: AUROC for detecting sabotage (full-experiments condition), best auditor
effect.value: Gemini 3.1 Pro AUROC=0.77, top-1 fix rate 42%, top-5 fix rate 53%

contradicts_or_qualifies: Notes that in most prior control evaluations, monitors of comparable capability to the attacker have been able to catch the attacker; this setting differs because attackers can retry sabotage ideas before committing, suggesting research sabotage may be a harder control setting than previously studied ones
stated_future_work: Excited about more work on human-constructed sabotages for research and other control settings
Study the harder threat model where an AI conducts novel research end-to-end, rather than sabotaging existing codebases
limitations_stated: With only 9 codebases adapted from existing papers, the benchmark is small and easy to overfit to
The setting differs from the harder threat model of an AI conducting novel research end-to-end
The red team (human) was allowed to retry sabotage ideas until one worked, a freedom a monitored AI would not have
quote: Our best auditor, Gemini 3.1 Pro, achieved an AUROC of 0.77 and a top-1 fix rate of 42%.
